Question B-006-012-003.

Why the correct answer is right: A free-space half-wave dipole has a doughnut-shaped three-dimensional pattern: maximum radiation around the sides of the wire and nulls off the ends.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "A major lobe off each end of the antenna": The ends of a half-wave dipole are the null directions. The major radiation is broadside to the wire.
- sourceIndex 2: "Spherical (equal radiation in all directions)": A spherical pattern is isotropic. A real half-wave dipole has directional maxima and nulls, so it is not equal in all directions.
- sourceIndex 3: "Major lobes at 45-degree angles to the antenna": Forty-five-degree lobes are not the free-space half-wave dipole pattern. The strongest radiation is broadside, at right angles to the wire.
